description: We are a passionate and creative team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are excited to explore space-related problems, develop innovative solutions, and learn together. We believe that teamwork, creativity, and scientific thinking are the keys to success. We are looking for motivated members with skills in programming, science, research, design, and problem-solving who are ready to share ideas and make a difference!
summary: We developed a browser-based 2D game that depicts the journey of NASA's Mars Opportunity rover. What we developed: a browser-based game you can play. It lets you drive a rover across terrain that changes every time based on Martian conditions. Dust storms and wind hazards are among the weather effects in the game that make the journey more difficult. Along the way players face quiz challenges about rover parts and mission facts. How it solves the problem: It takes science and space history and turns it into something fun and easy to understand. Learning by doing beats learning by reading or observing for players. This brings science and astronomy to life. It keeps the tale of the Mars Opportunity mission alive. It also shows that games can be more, than entertainment. They can teach, inspire and help people care about space and science.
details:
Project Details:

​What does it do and how does it work?

Our project is an interactive, browser-based 2D physics game titled "Opportunity Vehicle Journey". It simulates the historical mission of NASA’s Mars Opportunity rover. Players drive the rover across procedurally generated Martian terrain, managing fuel/water resources while navigating dynamic environmental challenges such as dust storms, wind hazards, and deep impact craters. Along the way, players encounter obstacles where they must answer educational trivia questions about the rover's actual spacecraft hardware and mission history. If a player runs out of fuel, falls into a deep crater, or answers a trivia question incorrectly, they must restart the current stage, adding an engaging survival and learning challenge.

​What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?

The project bridges the gap between entertainment and space education. Its primary benefit is making astronomy and planetary science accessible, engaging, and educational using gamification to teach real-world space exploration facts and reward perseverance.

​What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

​Languages: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (Vanilla ES6).

​Graphics & Physics: HTML5 Canvas API and custom 2D physics/terrain generation algorithms.

​Audio: Browser Native Web Audio API (procedural synthesis for engine hums, chimes, and sound effects without external media files).

​Environment: Developed and tested locally on modern web browsers across desktop and mobile platforms.

​How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider?

The project is creative because it transforms dry historical and engineering data into an interactive arcade-style survival game where failing trivia questions or mismanaging fuel has consequences, forcing the player to learn and adapt. Our team carefully considered accessibility, responsive design for mobile touch controls, user experience (UI/UX) with glassmorphism styling, and scientific accuracy regarding the Opportunity rover's actual instruments and mission parameters.
